"Today is a very happy day for us as Mutapa Gold Resources. It's the culmination of a process that began in April last year when we were threatened, as Freda Rebecca and as Bindura Town, with a shortage of water. "So we came up with the Masembura Water Pipeline Project. It means that security of water is no longer an issue for both ourselves as an operation and Bindura Town," he said.
The CEO explained that running a gold plant without water is impossible, noting that if they had not acted when Mwenje Dam dropped to 36 percent capacity last year, the whole plant would have closed.
"The reason why we ran around in April last year when Mwenje Dam was 36% was because we realised that if we ran out of water in Mwenje, we would actually close the plant.
"Without water, you can't run a gold processing plant. So it's very important,"added Shayawabaya.
Mashonaland Central Minister of State for Provincial Affairs and Devolution, Christopher Magomo, praised the development and the teamwork behind the project .
"We have commissioned it today on the 21st of September 2026. This is a milestone to Mashonaland Central Province as it adds up to our capital investment.
"And we look at this infrastructure actually giving value to our GDP and also looking at how it's going to help the citizens of Bindura Municipality.
"We'll be delighted if we see much more hours of water in our taps in Bindura.
"That would be a milestone. We are very happy also to see a partnership between a private player, Mutapa Gold Resources, and a local authority which has come to fruition today. Water is life, and this project is a huge relief for Bindura," he said.
As a booming mining hub experiencing rapid infrastructure growth and people moving from rural areas, the town desperately needed reliable water. This successful partnership proves how much it helps when big companies and local councils work together to bring clean water and a better life to the community.

title: India's infra push cuts travel time across key routes: From Delhi-Mumbai to Katra-Srinagar
content:
India's infra push cuts travel time across key routes: From Delhi-Mumbai to Katra-Srinagar
The introduction of Vande Bharat trains further enhances rail travel efficiency, showcasing significant advancements in connectivity nationwide.
India's expanding network of bridges, tunnels, expressways and faster trains is significantly reducing travel time across several major routes. In a detailed factsheet, PIB highlighted how infrastructure projects are cutting travel times by replacing longer routes, difficult terrain and river crossings with direct connections.
The factsheet cites examples from across the country, including the Delhi-Mumbai and Delhi-Dehradun corridors, the Atal Tunnel in Himachal Pradesh, bridges in the Northeast and new-generation Vande Bharat trains.
Delhi-Mumbai travel time to fall to about 12 hours
The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway is being developed to bring the road journey between the two cities down to about 12 hours from roughly 33 hours, according to the factsheet.
Other major expressways have already delivered substantial reductions.
The 82-km Delhi-Meerut Expressway has brought travel time between Delhi and Meerut down from around 2.5 hours to about 50 minutes. The 118-km Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway has reduced the journey from nearly three hours to about 75 minutes.

The recently developed Delhi-Dehradun Economic Corridor has reduced the journey from more than six hours to around 2.5 hours. The 213-km access-controlled corridor became operational in 2026.
The Mumbai-Nagpur Samruddhi Mahamarg has also substantially reduced travel time between the two cities, from about 16 hours to around eight hours.
The Ahmedabad-Dholera Expressway has reduced the Ahmedabad-Dholera journey from 100 km and 2 hours 15 minutes to 83 km and 45 minutes, while the Ahmedabad-Bhavnagar journey has fallen from 169 km and 3 hours 15 minutes to 141 km and 1 hour 45 minutes.
The Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway has also shortened key journeys. The first phase has reduced Delhi-Amritsar travel from eight hours to four hours and Delhi-Katra travel from 14 hours to six hours, according to the factsheet.
Bridges cut hours from journeys in Northeast, Bihar
Several bridge projects have transformed connectivity in regions where rivers and difficult terrain previously added hours to journeys.
The Bhupen Hazarika Setu, also known as the Dhola-Sadiya Bridge, reduced travel time between Rupai in Assam and Meka/Roing in Arunachal Pradesh from six hours to one hour, saving about five hours.
The Bogibeel Bridge over the Brahmaputra transformed connectivity between Dhemaji and Dibrugarh. Journeys that previously took almost an entire day now take about one to two hours.
In Bihar, the Kosi Rail Mahasetu reduced the rail journey between Nirmali and Saraigarh from about eight hours to 30 minutes. The rail distance was also reduced from around 300 km to 22 km.
The 200-metre Sisseri River Bridge in Arunachal Pradesh has cut travel time between Pasighat and Roing by about five hours, strengthening connectivity between the Dibang Valley and Siang regions.
Tunnels bypass difficult terrain
The factsheet also highlights tunnels that have shortened routes through mountainous regions.
The 9.02-km Atal Tunnel bypasses the Rohtang Pass, cuts the Manali-Sarchu distance by 46 km and saves four to five hours of travel. It also provides all-weather connectivity to Lahaul-Spiti.
The Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel in Jammu and Kashmir cuts the road distance by about 30 km and saves nearly two hours on the Jammu-Srinagar route. The 8.45-km Banihal-Qazigund twin-tube tunnel saves around 1.5 hours.
The Sela Tunnel in Arunachal Pradesh, built at an altitude of about 13,000 feet, has cut travel time on the Tezpur-Tawang route by more than an hour while providing all-weather connectivity.
Vande Bharat trains bring down rail travel time
The infrastructure push extends to railways, with newer trains and high-speed rail corridors aimed at reducing journey times.
The 2026 railway timetable saw 549 trains being speeded up. Of these, 20 trains gained 60 minutes or more, while 48 gained 31-59 minutes, 105 gained 16-30 minutes and 376 gained five to 15 minutes.
The New Delhi-Varanasi Vande Bharat Express, launched in February 2019, takes approximately eight hours on the route and is described in the factsheet as around 40-50% faster than earlier services.
More recent Vande Bharat services have produced further time savings. The Katra-Srinagar service has cut the journey to about three hours, while the extended Jammu-Srinagar service covers the journey in 4 hours 50 minutes. The Banaras-Khajuraho service saves about 2 hours 40 minutes, while the Ernakulam-Bengaluru service saves more than two hours.
The first Vande Bharat Sleeper service between Howrah and Guwahati has reduced the journey from about 17 hours to around 14 hours, saving nearly three hours compared with the Saraighat Express.

Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train targeted for 2027
The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor is expected to bring another major reduction in travel time. The 508-km corridor is designed for an operational speed of 320 kmph and is expected to bring the journey down to about 1 hour 58 minutes, compared with eight to nine hours by road.
The corridor will have 12 stations and includes a roughly 7-km undersea rail tunnel beneath Thane Creek. The first service is targeted for August 2027.
Seven additional high-speed rail corridors announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 are expected to span nearly 4,000 km, with an estimated investment of ₹16 lakh crore. The indicative travel times include around 3 hours 50 minutes between Delhi and Varanasi, 2 hours between Bengaluru and Hyderabad, 48 minutes between Mumbai and Pune and 1 hour 55 minutes between Pune and Hyderabad.
The factsheet presents the infrastructure expansion through the time saved on everyday journeys, arguing that bridges, tunnels, expressways and modern rail services are reducing the constraints imposed by distance and improving connectivity between regions.
Separately, the government has said the national highway network reached 1,46,572 km by March 2026, up from 91,287 km in FY2014, while four-lane and wider national highways increased to 45,516 km from 18,371 km in 2014.

title: Bert Schulpen (94) maakt al 80 jaar muziek, even lang als de academie van Maaseik bestaat
content:
Bert Schulpen hoorde in 1946 bij de eerste leerlingen van de academie van Maaseik. Tot voor kort speelde hij nog muziek in het woonzorgcentrum waar hij nu woont. Hij verzorgt morgen als oudste ex-leerling het voorwoord van de viering van 80 jaar kunstonderwijs in Maaseik.
Bert Schulpen (94) maakt al 80 jaar muziek, even lang als de academie van Maaseik bestaat
Bert Schulpen kreeg net na de oorlog een trompet van Amerikaanse soldaten, die het instrument in Duitsland hadden gehaald. "Zo ben ik beginnen te oefenen", vertelt hij. Toen in Maaseik een muziekschool opgericht werd, was Schulpen daar een van de eerste leerlingen.
"We waren toen met 36, er waren 2 klassen." De lessen gingen door in de stadsfeestzaal op de Markt, met notenleer van Mientje Loyen uit Molenbeersel en later ook van Kris Steegen.
Enkele jaren later sloot Schulpen zich aan bij de harmonie Concordia, waar ook zijn broers deel van uitmaakten. Daar speelde hij verschillende instrumenten: trompet, bugel, saxofoon, tuba en bombardon. Tussendoor trad hij ook op met een accordeonist en een drummer op kermissen in de buurt.
Muziek in Congo
Als para-commando speelde Schulpen tijdens zijn legerdienst in Congo in een orkestje, samen met enkele Limburgers en iemand uit Kortrijk. "We traden op voor hogere officieren in Kamina, in hotel La Gare. We kregen toen 1.000 frank per optreden."
De uitbater van het hotel kocht zelfs instrumenten voor de muzikanten, die ze later moesten teruggeven, toen ze terugkeerden naar België.
Maaseiker Blaaskapel
Schulpen was 36 jaar lid van de Maaseiker Blaaskapel. "We zijn begonnen met die blaaskapel, vanuit enkele muzikanten van de harmonie", vertelt Schulpen.
Toen de blaaskapel geld begon te verdienen, wilde de voorzitter van de harmonie dat ze dat zouden afstaan aan de vereniging. Dat leidde tot een conflict, waarna de meeste leden, onder wie Schulpen en zijn 2 broers, ontslag namen bij de harmonie. Als blaaskapel speelden ze daarna veel optredens, tot in Oostenrijk.
In totaal maakte Schulpen ruim 80 jaar muziek. Tot voor enige tijd speelde hij nog in het woonzorgcentrum waar hij verblijft, op het terras of op zijn kamer. Hij speelde er uiteenlopende muziek, van moderne stukken tot carnavalsmuziek, en zong vaak mee aan de deur van zijn kamer.
Viering 80 jaar stedelijke academie voor Kunsten
Zaterdagavond doet Bert Schulpen het voorwoord bij de viering van 80 jaar Stedelijke Academie voor Kunsten. Dat wordt een groot spektakel vol muziek, woord, beeld en dans. Directeur John Vandecaetsbeek: "Alle kunstvormen die we aanbieden, gaan we samenbrengen op een podium en daarbij het verhaal van 80 jaar geschiedenis vertellen. Er staan meer dan 300 mensen op het podium."
De voorstelling Art in Motion is zaterdag om 19.00 uur in de Steengoed Arena in Maaseik.

title: Wachsendes Interesse an Sozialprojekt „Zeitpolster“
content:
Das Motto von „Zeitpolster“ ist „Wir machen möglich, was früher selbstverständlich war" – nämlich Hilfe für Menschen, die darauf angewiesen sind, so Birgit Wurzwallner von „Zeitpolster“ in der Steiermark.
Einkaufen oder in die Oper gehen
"Einerseits, wenn eine ältere Dame zum Arzt alleine nicht hinkommt, dass man mit ihr gemeinsam hingeht, oder wir haben eine Anfrage gekriegt: Einfach einmal die Vorhänge runternehmen und wieder aufhängen, nachdem sie gewaschen wurden“, so Wurzwallner.
Pflege und Reinigungsarbeiten zählen nicht zu den Aufgabengebieten, aber: „Einkaufen gehen oder zusammen in die Oper gehen. Der Mann ist verstorben, und die 90-jährige Dame möchte aber noch gerne in die Oper und hat niemanden“, erklärt Wurzwallner.
Eigene Zeit wieder für sich einlösen
Jede geleistete Stunde in solchen kleinen oder größeren Hilfeleistungen wird dem eigenen „Zeitpolster“-Konto gutgeschrieben und kann später über das Netzwerk eingelöst werden. Die Idee ist nicht nur einfach, sie kann den Unterschied in der Lebenssituation der Menschen machen, die die Hilfe in Anspruch nehmen, so Wurzwallner: „Manchmal sind es einfach solche Kleinigkeiten, die es ausmachen, dass jemand noch länger daheim bleiben kann."
Es gehe um die Frage, „was brauchen wir als Gesellschaft, damit Nachbarschaftshilfe wieder gut funktionieren kann, und dass es ein Miteinander gibt? Und andererseits: Was kann ich als Person heute für mich tun, damit ich Unterstützung kriege, wenn ich sie selbst einmal brauche?"
Zu den etwa 250 Helfenden in der Steiermark kommen gerade laufend mehr dazu. Zuletzt sind zwei Gemeindegruppen neu gegründet worden – fünf sind es mittlerweile, Feldbach und Liezen sollen bald dazukommen.

title: ‘America has been great to me but I see the world through my Irish eyes’
content:
Elaine Brennan was one of the lucky recipients of a Morrison visa that enabled her to embark on a career in the US in 1994. The Ennis-born life science graduate feels she has benefited enormously from that privilege, so when the opportunity came to thank the man who paved an early path for her, she didn’t hesitate.
Brennan, who holds a senior position at Northwell Health, the largest private employer in the state of New York, was at a dinner in the city three years ago hosted by the consul general which included a select group of Irish-born business figures, as well as the Taoiseach.
“I asked every one of these people around the table how they had come to America. The overwhelming response was that it was through the Morrison visa. Something clicked in me and I wondered was there any way we could thank him,” she says.
Loretta Brennan Glucksman, the prominent Irish-American philanthropist, was also at the table. She knew the former congressman Bruce Morrison and offered to make an introduction. This proved the seed for a foundation named in his honour.
READ MORE
The Morrison visa programme created a specific allocation over a three-year period for nationals from countries that were underrepresented in US immigration. Some 40 per cent of these visas were designated for Irish immigrants from both sides of the Border, resulting in 45,000 people from the island securing access to a life in the US.
The Morrison Legacy Foundation’s aims are to document the programme’s history, analyse its social impact and foster a deeper appreciation of the shared heritage between Ireland and the US through partnerships with cultural and educational institutes.
Morrison was honoured at the foundation’s inaugural gala dinner last year. “It was really important for me to acknowledge him while he is still alive. He serves on our board and is as sharp as a tack,” Brennan says.
Brennan’s three-decade career in the US has seen her pivot several times, but life science has been a common thread. She landed first in Florida and soon moved on to a position in Boston, often working late into the evening in a laboratory, publishing scientific papers, filing patents and lecturing one day a week in MIT.
[ ‘It would take a lot to bring me home now’Opens in new window ]
She enjoys telling the story of how she had filed a patent for a biodegradable confectionery product and the cheque she received that day was from a household-name brand to buy the patent for the princely sum of $5. While not uncommon, it proved a turning point for her.
“I knew there was a better path for me. I ripped up the cheque, booked a Greyhound to New York and crashed with my friend Mary.”
Brennan didn’t have a new job lined up but knew she wanted to work in the commercial end of the life science business. Securing a job there proved elusive at first. “This was the era before email was prevalent and I remember mailing about 100 résumés to companies and not a single response. I was applying for business development roles, but they just saw me as a lab rat.”
Taking what she admits was a more calculated approach to the task, the Clare woman took a job as a doctor’s receptionist, knowing that would put her in regular contact with drug company reps. The gamble paid off. “The doctor I worked with pulled me into his office one day and said ‘I don’t think this is the career for you’ but by that stage I had a job lined up at Roche.”
Brennan threw herself into the role there, working in infectious diseases area, including a major HIV drug. Although a devastating disease, Brennan says it was also a very exciting time to be working in this area as the team she worked with could see the major breakthroughs that were happening in treatment. She was also involved in the marketing launch of a very successful hepatitis drug called Pegasys.
When an opportunity presented itself to work with Enterprise Ireland running its life sciences division in the US, she jumped at the chance. While it involved a significant drop in salary and benefits, Brennan was excited by the prospect of helping Irish companies achieve success in the US market. It also developed a network of contacts that helps her to this day. Among her notable achievements in this role was successfully promoting Ireland as a leading centre of excellence for gastroenterology.
[ Intercountry hurler scores big in New York construction sectorOpens in new window ]
Her last pivot was to Northwell Health, which has 28 hospitals, over 105,000 employees and 1,000 care locations in New York state. As executive director of its global strategic partnerships team, she has responsibility for developing collaborative and strategic relationships, including creating opportunities for early-stage companies with the established pharma and biotech industries.
Reflecting again on the opportunities presented to her by her access to the United States via the visa, she says: “America has been great to me, and I feel I have two loyalties, but I see the world through my Irish eyes. I get back to Ireland as often as I can and unlike people who have gone to more far-flung places such as Australia, it’s very easy to get back to Ireland from here, even for a weekend.”
She is busy helping to plan the foundation’s second gala, which takes place later this month and will honour publisher Niall O’Dowd for his significant contributions to the Irish-American community and his role in the Northern Ireland peace process.
Downtime is spent playing tennis and vacationing in a holiday home in Florida. Brennan also enjoys all of the attractions of living in the Big Apple.
“New York is a city of contrasts. You have immense wealth and extreme hardship. You’ve got the global influences and the deeply local neighbourhoods. You can be as individual as you want but you can also belong to whatever community you want. I have friends across many nationalities, as well as my Irish ones.”

title: Japanese teen sets world record weeks after COVID-19 recovery
content:
Japanese teenager Shin Ohashi has set a new world record in the men’s 200m breaststroke at the Asian Games, just weeks after recovering from COVID-19.
As reported by BBC Sport on Thursday, the 17-year-old stormed to gold in a time of 2:04.83, comfortably breaking the previous world record of 2:05.48 set by China’s Qin Haiyang at the 2023 World Championships.
Ohashi admitted that contracting COVID-19 caused some mental anxiety during his preparations, but said the recovery period also gave his body a chance to properly rest.
“Regarding Covid, after all, there was a part where it created a little anxiety for me mentally,” Ohashi said after his victory. “But, conversely, physically I think it was good that I was able to properly rest my body as a period of recovery.”
The world-record performance was Ohashi’s second gold medal of the Games. Earlier in the competition, he shared the 100m breaststroke title with China’s Dong Zhihao.
Ohashi has been regarded as one of swimming’s brightest young talents.
He won five gold medals at the World Junior Championships last year, while French Olympic champion Léon Marchand previously described the Japanese youngster as a “scary” prospect.
His record-breaking performance adds another chapter to an impressive Asian Games campaign and establishes Ohashi as a major name to watch in international swimming.
Meanwhile, China’s Zhang Zhanshuo, 19, claimed his sixth gold medal of the Games as China won the men’s 4x100m freestyle relay.

title: Lapset | Syömiseen on aikaa alle 15 minuuttia Katajanokan ala-asteella
content:
”Sano joku kahdella a-kirjaimella alkava sana?”
Katajanokan ala-asteen 1. luokka on kerääntynyt jonoksi ruokalan oville. Kello on 10.40.
Jokainen pääsee vuorollaan sisään ovista. Ovella luokanopettaja Jarmo Rautio kysyy jokaiselta vaihtuvilla kirjaimilla alkavaa sanaa. Sisälle pääsee, kun keksii sopivan sanan.
Ruokailuun on aikaa 15 minuuttia. Koska osa ajasta kuluu ruuan hakemiseen, jää syömiseen varattu aika vielä lyhyemmäksi.
Kello 10.45 kaikki ovat päässet linjastolle, pöytiin 10.47. Lounaana on tänään silakkamurekepihvejä ja härkäpapupihvejä.
Pian opettaja kuikuilee ruokalasalin ovilta. Rautio elehtii hänelle sormillaan, että ”noin 10 minuuttia”.
Katajanokan koulussa ensimmäisen luokan ruokailu on osa kolmatta oppituntia. 1. luokan ensimmäiset kaksi oppituntia pidetään putkeen kello 8.30–10.
Aamutuntien jälkeen on puolen tunnin mittainen välitunti, ja seuraava tunti alkaa 10.30.
Raution mukaan oppituntiin on varattu aikaa 60 minuuttia, josta 15 minuuttia on varattu lounastauon pitämiseen, kertoo Jarmo Rautio.
Pienessä ruokatilassa vallitsee rauhallinen puheensorina.
Raution mukaan 15 minuuttia riittää ylempien luokkien oppilaille yleensä varsin mainiosti, mutta pienemmillä lapsilla syömiseen kuluu herkästi enemmän aikaa.
”Alussa tämä on tietysti opettelua kaikki.”
Tarvittaessa oppilas saa lisää aikaa.
Tuleeko kiire?
”Välillä, jos ottaa liikaa ruokaa”, kommentoi kalapihviään viipaloiva tyttö.
”Mutta yleensä ei. Yleensä ehdin aika hyvin takas luokkaan”, hän jatkaa.
Monella oppilaalla on ranteessaan älykello, jota osa vilkuilee melko tiuhaankin tahtiin samoin kuin seinällä olevaa seinäkelloa.
”Viisi minuuttia jäljellä”, yhdestä pöydästä huudahtaa annostaan viimeistelevä tyttö. Hän sanoo, että hänestä ei kuitenkaan tunnu siltä, että ruokailussa olisi liian kiire.
Myös poikien neljän hengen pöydässä ollaan sitä mieltä, että aikaa syömiseen on aivan tarpeeksi.
Ekaluokkalaisen Max Laitasalo Kekkosen ja hänen pöytäseurueensa pöydässä käy hyväntuulinen puheensorina. Heidän mielestään aikaa syömiseen on riittävästi.
Kun ”viisari on ykkösen kohdalla”, tässä tapauksessa viisi yli 11, niin pitää lähteä, eräs seurueesta ohjeistaa.
Eniten Laitasalo Kekkosta ja hänen seuruettaan tuntuu harmittavan melu. Lapset kertovat, että heitä on ohjeistettu, että ruokalassa pitäisi olla rauhallisesti. Oman pöytäseurueen kesken saa jutella, mutta viereisiin pöytiin ei sopisi huudella.
Kello alkaa lähestyä yhtätoista.
”Teillä on tänään pöytien pyyhintävuoro”, Jarmo Rautio huikkaa paikaltaan ja osoittaa kolmea eri oppilasta. Laitasalo Kekkonen on yksi heistä.
Suurin osa nousee pöydistä 11.05 ja menee palauttamaan astiansa.
Syömään kuitenkin jää vielä muutama tyttö. He saavat syödä loppuun rauhassa. Samalla toiset oppilaat pyyhkivät pöytiä ja toiset nostelevat tuoleja pöytälevyjen alla oleviin telineisiin.
Viimeisetkin saavat viimeisteltyä ruokailunsa 11.08.
Suunnitellusta huolimatta ainakin pienimpien oppilaiden ruokailuun kuluu väistämättä lähes perinteisen puolen tunnin lounastunnin verran aikaa.
Järjestely puhuttaa vanhempia.
”Miksei oppilaille ole varattu erillisiä ruokatunteja, jottei ruokailu sijoittuisi oppitunneille?” ihmettelee Maxin äiti, Anni Laitasalo Kekkonen.
Asia herätti oppilaiden vanhemmissa huolta ensimmäisen luokan vanhempainillan jälkeen.
”Haluaisimme, että olisi rauha ruokailuun ja oikeus oppimiseen.”
Jos ruokailu venyy sille suunnitellusta 15 minuutista, kärsii opetus, hän ajattelee.
Miksi kouluruokailu on oppitunnin päällä, Katajanokan ala-asteen rehtori Marko Sirén?
”Se on aikataulutettu niin, että kaikki ehtii syömään, eli kolmessa ryhmässä syödään, ja niin, että keittiö ehtii laittamaan ruuan valmiiksi aina seuraavalle ryhmälle. Siksi on aikataulutettu näin.”
Jos 60 minuutin oppitunnista on varattu 15 minuuttia syömiselle ja ruokailu venyy, niin eikö se syö sitä oppituntia?
”Näinhän se tekee. Mutta me katsomme, että se on arjen taitojen oppimista, että oppilaat harjoittelevat jonottamista, pesevät kädet ja kuorivat perunoita. Ruokailuaika itsessään on se 15 minuuttia, tai aika lähelle sen.”
Sirénin mukaan ensimmäisten luokkien opetus on kokonaisvaltaista, ja tunnit usein ikään kuin sekoittuvat toisiinsa.
”Voi esimerkiksi olla matematiikkatuokio ja sitten opettaja lukee lapsille kirjaa. Ei se mene ihan niin, että on 45 minuuttia yhtä oppiainetta ja 45 minuuttia toista ihan tiukasti.”
Oppiaineet eivät siis ole niin tarkkarajaisia, vaikka lukujärjestys pitääkin Sirénin mukaan teknisistä syistä tehdä niin, että siellä näkyvät kaikki oppitunnit.
”15 minuutin lounas kuulostaa ongelmalta”, opetusneuvos Marjaana Manninen Opetushallituksesta (OPH).
Kolmanneksessa tutkituista kouluista ruokailuaikaa oli 25 minuuttia, selvisi OPH:n ja Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitoksen tutkimuksessa. Yli puolessa kouluista ruokailuun oli aikaa 16–25 minuuttia, ja 12 prosentissa kouluista vain 10–15 minuuttia.
Kouluruokailun tulisi OPH:n mukaan olla kiireetön osa koulupäivää. Liian nopeasti syöminen aiheuttaa haasteita ruuansulatukselle ja aivojen kylläisyyskeskukselle.
”Liian nopeasti syöminen aiheuttaa haasteita kylläisyyden tunnistamiselle, sillä elimistön kylläisyyssignaalien välittyminen vie aikaa.”
Jos jo koulussa tottuu syömään nopealla tahdilla kelloa katsoen, siitä tulee helposti tapa, joka säilyy aikuisuuteen saakka.
”Mitä useammin joku asia toistuu, niin sitä vahvemmin siitä tulee opittu tapa. Tämähän tarkoittaa sitä, että opimme hotkimaan ja syömään liian paljon tai liian vähän, ja ateriarytmi häiriintyy.”

title: Scholastica 2026 ends on high note
content:
Judith Phiri [email protected]
SCHOLASTICA 2026 ended on a high note on Friday bringing together thousands of students from schools across Bulawayo, Matabeleland North, Matabeleland South and the Midlands for career guidance, skills development and exposure to opportunities in different professions.
Organised by the Zimbabwe International Trade Fair (ZITF) Company at the Zimbabwe International Conference and Exhibition Smart City (ZICES), the three-day education, careers and training expo ran under the theme: “RISE – Ready, Inspired, Skilled, Empowered.”
It provided students with an opportunity to interact with professionals, entrepreneurs and industry experts while exploring career pathways in the arts and humanities, commerce and the sciences.
More than 4 000 students participated during the first two days of the programme, highlighting the growing demand for career guidance initiatives that help young people make informed decisions about their education and future professions.
In an interview ZITF Company Marketing and Corporate Communications Manager on Thursday, Mr Thandolwenkosi Nkomo said the first day focused on careers in the arts, sport and humanities, with activities designed to showcase opportunities within the creative industries.
“Among the highlights was a fashion show that demonstrated how creativity and talent can be transformed into viable career and business opportunities.
“The second day shifted attention to careers within the commercial sector, featuring panel discussions and presentations aimed at exposing students to opportunities in business and related professions. Entrepreneurs and other professionals shared their experiences and insights with learners,” he said.
“The programme concluded with a focus on science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), with workshops and seminars that gave students greater insight into careers in science and technology.”
He said through the different sessions, Scholastica 2026 sought to bridge the gap between classroom learning and the world of work by giving students access to practical career information and professionals already operating in various sectors.
Mr Nkomo said the event also provided a platform for students from different schools and provinces to interact, exchange ideas and broaden their understanding of the career opportunities available to them.
“The conclusion of Scholastica 2026 leaves participating students with greater exposure to diverse career pathways and information that could assist them as they make decisions about further education, skills development and their future careers.”
Ministry of Youth Empowerment, Development and Vocational Training Administrative Officer and Acting Zimbabwe Youth Council (ZYC) Bulawayo Province Manager, Ms Nqobile Bodma drawing on her extensive background as a trained educator shared vital national initiatives designed to foster youth development and vocational growth.
“Students must cultivate an entrepreneurial mindset focused on creating genuine value, emphasising that the future of work is inextricably linked with technology. We encourage you to explore emerging digital opportunities, utilise technology responsibly, and master financial literacy to secure their personal and professional success.”
From Botswana, Ba Isago University Manager for Business Development, Ms Tshegofatso Kgetse, highlighted the incredible global study opportunities available at their institution.
“We have diverse academic programmes and student-friendly approaches that including flexible Untied State Dollars (USD) tuition fee payment structures tailored for international scholars.”
As familiar faces at the ZICES having previously exhibited during the annual ZITF Show, the university continues to build strong educational bridges, opening doors for local students to pursue world-class tertiary qualifications.
A sizable number of exhibitors featured at Scholastica 2026, with two universities from Botswana and India. Among the exhibitors were private and public sector organisations and non-governmental organisations (NGOs).

title: Clinical usefulness of objective tongue image devices monitoring in temporal tongue color: a demonstration of successively treated cases with traditional medicines
content: BackgroundIn Kampo medicine (traditional Japanese medicine), the diagnostic method of observing a patient's tongue is called the ‘tongue diagnosis’. Information provided by observation of a patient's tongue is used to help select prescriptions at the initial consultation, monitor treatment effectiveness after therapy begins, and determine whether prescriptions should be changed. Kampo practitioners must therefore accurately compare the patient's past tongue condition with the current condition. However, it can be difficult to remember the precise details regarding a patient's previous tongue's appearance and to consistently make accurate comparisons. Given the need for objective and reproducible method of documenting tongue findings, we investigated the usefulness of our developed Tongue Image Analyzing System (TIAS). The application of the TIAS for two representative patients is described herein.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent tongue photography after providing informed consent and selected two cases with contrasting degrees of longitudinal changes in tongue findings. One patient demonstrated subtle changes in tongue color that were difficult to detect with the naked eye, and the other patient showed marked tongue color changes accompanied by changes in the heterogeneity of the tongue coating. We obtained the tongue color values in each case from tongue images photographed by TIAS as RGB data and converted into the CIE L*a*b* color space.ResultsThe tongue color of case1 was analyzed at three time points. The color difference from the first consultation (calculated as ΔE00 using L*a*b* values) increased by ΔE00 1–2 after 42 days. This change was too subtle to be perceived by the naked eye. The tongue color of case 2, tongue color was analyzed at five time points. The color difference between the first consultation and 105 days later was ΔE00 10.08, indicating a substantial change in tongue color.ConclusionTIAS enables standardized longitudinal tongue imaging and facilitates the objective and quantitative comparison of subtle changes in tongue color that may be difficult to discern visually. These findings suggest that TIAS may be useful for objectively documenting and comparing longitudinal changes in tongue findings in clinical practice.
